title: Commission full-range control of a gravity-drained tank
equipment: Vented gravity-drained water tank with variable-speed inlet pump
principalTechnique: Validated local models and atomically interpolated PI gain scheduling
objective: Prove the limitation of one fixed PI, qualify three local tank models, and validate one tracked gain-scheduled PI across the complete operating envelope without applying revision 80.
physicalPurpose: Maintain liquid level consistently while square-root gravity outflow changes plant gain and response time with operating level.

simplifications: The vertical tank has constant area, is well mixed, and drains through one fixed square-root gravity outlet.
The ideal variable-speed pump follows bounded applied flow without pump-curve, inlet-pressure, drive, valve, or pipe dynamics.
The three tangent models are local approximations and do not replace the nonlinear balance globally.
Overflow, cavitation, foam, density changes, sensor lag, independent trips, and functional safety are outside the model.
All executable results are Simulation evidence and do not authorize a physical pump.

baseline.limitation: The conservative high-level integral gain is unnecessarily slow in the low-level region.

change.decision: Accept scheduling only when all local models and the scheduling variable are qualified, the common full-range requirements improve, and boundaries plus authority transitions remain deterministic and bumpless.

disturbances: Request 0.55 m at 30 seconds, 0.80 m at 120 seconds, 0.55 m at 240 seconds, and 0.30 m at 330 seconds.
Identify separately restored local models at 0.30, 0.55, and 0.80 m using bounded pump pulses and unused validation records.

Exercise deterministic sensor noise at interpolation points, invalid level quality, invalid schedule, unavailable pump, Manual tracking and return, an out-of-envelope request, ControlledStop, restoration, and rollback.

acceptance.window: worst of four eligible transitions from 30 through 420 seconds

abortPredicates: Required level, setpoint, flow, quality, availability, scheduling, mode, or timing data are nonfinite, stale, invalid, or outside the declared envelope.
Measured level leaves 0.20 through 0.90 m or requested/applied pump flow leaves 0 through 0.060 m3/s.
The scheduled record is invalid, clamped, mixed, or used outside its validated local-model envelope.
The selected pump is unavailable, tracking disagrees with applied flow, or authority return exceeds 0.0005 m3/s.
Revision 80 changes without separate explicit application approval.
Simulation evidence is presented as overflow, dry-running, pump-protection, functional-safety, or physical commissioning evidence.
safety.restorationMode: Close the simulated pump, restore qualified level and scheduling data plus pump availability, align the inactive controller to measured applied flow, restore the tank inside the validated envelope, then explicitly re-enter Automatic.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process-control engineer with tank, pump, piping, electrical, operations, environmental, and functional-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not operate a physical tank, pump, valve, or drain from this lesson.
Physical experiments require independently reviewed overflow, dry-run, capacity, isolation, topology, limits, excitation, abort, restoration, approval, and rollback immediately before action.
Applying revision 80 requires separate explicit approval and a rollback-ready commissioning window.

video.viewerOutcome: Commission and defend one full-range level strategy from nonlinear balance through local-model scheduling and tracked recovery.

learning.context: Two equivalent vented tanks receive bounded one-sided inlet-pump flow and drain through the same nonlinear square-root gravity outlet.
learning.reason: A fixed PI qualified high in the tank is measured to be unnecessarily slow low in the tank because local gain and response time change with level.
theory: Mass conservation and square-root outflow produce operating-point-dependent local first-order dynamics.
Local identification and independent validation establish where each tangent model may support a controller design.
A qualified requested level schedules one complete interpolated parameter record for a retained PI state.
Requested and applied pump flow, authority tracking, schedule validity, and physical limits remain separate.
learning.workedPrediction: At 0.30, 0.55, and 0.80 m, equilibrium flows are 0.02739, 0.03708, and 0.04472 m3/s; local gains and time constants are 21.91, 29.66, and 35.78 in their declared units.
practicalPreparation: Declare equipment, nonlinear balance, units, schedule envelope, quality, pump authority, modes, limits, aborts, rollback, and Simulation evidence class.
Predict fixed and scheduled regional behavior before running the common record.
learning.baseline: Run the conservative high-level fixed PI through the complete low-middle-high-middle-low sequence and retain its regional limitation.
learning.change: Change only the integral gain through one filtered, atomically applied schedule built from three accepted local models.
learning.comparison: Classify evidence eligibility before comparing regional IAE, departure, pump movement, parameter continuity, authority return, limits, and faults.
learning.validation: Validate the nominal range, deterministic noise, local-model uncertainty, invalid quality and schedule, unavailable pump, Manual return, out-of-envelope rejection, ControlledStop, restoration, and unchanged revision.
learning.explanation: Trace operating level through nonlinear outflow, local dynamics, qualified scheduling, retained PI state, requested flow, applied pump authority, level response, and recovery.
learning.transfer: Lesson 81 retains local-model discipline but introduces transport delay that can consume stability margin even when gains are locally appropriate.
